(سَفَطَ) السِّينُ وَالْفَاءُ وَالطَّاءُ لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ، وَمَا فِي بَابِهِ مَا يُعَوَّلُ عَلَيْهِ، إِلَّا أَنَّهُمْ سَمُّوا هَذَا السَّفَطَ. وَيَقُولُونَ: السَّفِيطُ السَّخِيُّ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ. وَأَنْشَدُوا:
لَيْسَ بِذِي حَزْمٍ وَلَا سَفِيطِ
وَهَذَا لَيْسَ بِشَيْءٍ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: سَفَّطَ • (saffaṭa) II (non-past يُسَفِّطُ (yusaffiṭu), verbal noun تَسْفِيط (tasfīṭ))
سَفَط • (safaṭ) m (plural أَسْفَاط (ʔasfāṭ))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Interrelated with the roots ش ف ط (š f ṭ), س ف ف (s f f) and ش ف ف (š f f) meaning "to take something into one's mouth", "to lick up"; "to render lean or emaciate", "to leave emptied or exhausted"; both roots feature the meaning "to drink up much water". The /ط/ is perhaps a dialectal variant of verb form VIII إشْتَفَّ (ʔištaffa, “to drink all that is in a vessel, drinking to last drop, to drink without satisfying thirst; to die, to be drained of one's measure of life”).
